verdicts.note: IMSLP lists only 1834 autograph manuscripts (full score, piano score, violin part; "first publication 2025" = scan upload); no printed edition and not in the Wikipedia work list. Juvenile manuscript-only piece.

IMSLP: Air varié avec introduction ... de l'opéra Il Pirata de Bellini, Op. 6 (Artaria, Vienna 1837); Wikipedia list agrees (Op. 6 number also clashes with the song "Le chevalier"). "Il" was flagged only because IMSLP's OCR text reads "Jl Pirata".

verdicts.title: Andante et Rondo in E major, Op. 29
verdicts.note: Published by Schuberth (Leipzig, 1853) as Op. 29 and so listed on IMSLP, but Op. 29 is also used for the 3 Verdi Fantasies; the Wikipedia list numbers the Andante et rondo Op. 28 (key E major). Kept IMSLP/publisher number; owner may prefer Op. 28 to avoid a duplicate opus.
IMSLP: Bouquet américain, Op. 33, six pieces on American tunes (Schuberth, Leipzig 1860, plate 2538); Wikipedia agrees Op. 33.

verdicts.title: Capriccio "Les arpèges", Op. 15
verdicts.note: IMSLP work title is Capriccio 'Les Arpèges' (Troupenas, Paris [1843], plate T 1454; Artaria violin-piano edition); Wikipedia: "Les arpèges", Caprice, Op. 15.
IMSLP: "Chansons russes de Werstofsky. Transcrites et variées", key C, violin & piano, 1852 (Werstofsky = Verstovsky); Wikipedia lists it without opus.
IMSLP: Six divertissements d'amateurs sur des thèmes russes, Op. 24 (1852); Wikipedia agrees (Op. 24 number also used for the Camp de Silésie duo).
IMSLP: Duo brillant, Op. 39, A major, 3 movements, violin + cello (or viola) with orchestra (1864), piano reduction exists. Second soloist may be cello or viola.
IMSLP: Fantasia on themes from Gounod's Faust; Wikipedia: Fantasie on Faust (1869), violin & piano/orchestra, dedicated to Wilma Norman-Neruda; no opus number.
IMSLP: Fantaisie sur 'Norma', Op. 18 (Schuberth, Hamburg 1845); Wikipedia subtitle "Fantaisie sur la quatrième corde". Not the same as Variations on Norma, Op. 2.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Op. 54 = Saltarelle; Sérénade; Pochade américaine (Brandus c.1883).
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Op. 54 No. 2 Sérénade.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Op. 54 No. 3 Pochade américaine.

verdicts.title: Fantaisie sur 'I Lombardi', Op. 29 No. 1
verdicts.note: IMSLP "3 Fantaisies sur les opéras de Verdi, Op.29" (1852): three separately published fantasies, Schott (Mainz) [1852], plate 11494, dedicated to Mme Édouard Wolff. Title in the draft mixed French and English; IMSLP and Wikipedia give only the opera names. Note Op. 29 is also given to the Andante et rondo (see N3).

verdicts.title: Fantaisie sur 'Ernani', Op. 29 No. 2
verdicts.note: IMSLP "3 Fantaisies sur les opéras de Verdi, Op.29" (1852): three separately published fantasies, Schott (Mainz) [1852], plate 11546, dedicated to Mlle Theresa Milanollo. Title in the draft mixed French and English; IMSLP and Wikipedia give only the opera names. Note Op. 29 is also given to the Andante et rondo (see N3).

verdicts.title: Fantaisie sur 'Luisa Miller', Op. 29 No. 3
verdicts.note: IMSLP "3 Fantaisies sur les opéras de Verdi, Op.29" (1852): three separately published fantasies, Escudier (Paris), plate B.C. 1298, later Schott London; dedicated to Mme Bedier. Title in the draft mixed French and English; IMSLP and Wikipedia give only the opera names. Note Op. 29 is also given to the Andante et rondo (see N3).

verdicts.title: Romance in F major, Op. 40 No. 1
verdicts.note: Wikipedia list: Op. 40 = Romance en fa majeur; Les regrets; Bohémienne (IMSLP: Romance; Regrets; Bohémienne; 1864).
IMSLP: Regrets (Wikipedia: "Les regrets").
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Bohémienne (also arranged for violin & orchestra as Airs bohémiens, Op. 40a).
IMSLP: Grand Duo sur 'Le Prophète', Op. 26 (Duo concertante No. 5; 1849/50), violin & piano; Wikipedia agrees Op. 26.

IMSLP: Grand Duo sur 'Orphée' (on themes of Gluck), violin & piano, co-authored with Édouard Wolff, Schott Mainz plate 17556, dedicated to Mme Érard; Wikipedia lists it without opus as "Duo brillant sur Orphée" (1864).
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Hommage à Paganini, caprice, Op. 9 (violin & piano; orchestral version arr.).
IMSLP/Wikipedia: 3 Märchen, Op. 34 = Hausmärchen; Kindermärchen; Wintermärchen (Schuberth, Hamburg 1859). No. 1 Hausmärchen.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: 3 Märchen, Op. 34 = Hausmärchen; Kindermärchen; Wintermärchen (Schuberth, Hamburg 1859). No. 2 Kindermärchen.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: 3 Märchen, Op. 34 = Hausmärchen; Kindermärchen; Wintermärchen (Schuberth, Hamburg 1859). No. 3 Wintermärchen.

IMSLP/Wikipedia: 6 Morceaux de salon, Op. 22 = Morceau brillant de salon; Air varié; Rêverie; Souvenir du Bosphore; Tarantelle; L'Orage (Bote & Bock c.1846-52). No. 6 L'Orage is missing from the catalogue (see gaps).

verdicts.title: Air varié in D minor, Op. 22 No. 2
verdicts.note: Wikipedia list: "Air varié en ré mineur" (IMSLP: Air varié; Bote & Bock [1847]; Schott).
IMSLP: Souvenir du Bosphore, Op. 22 No. 4 (Schott).
IMSLP: 3 Morceaux de salon, Op. 32 = Souvenir de Beauchamps; Rondino; La Chasse (Brandus 1856).
IMSLP: Op. 32 No. 3 La Chasse (also a version for solo violin / violin and winds, Op. 32a).

IMSLP: Six Morceaux, Op. 55, solo violin (Andante; Moderato; Prélude; Tempo di minuetto; Andante; Introduction et fugue). Wikipedia notes number clashes (Op. 55 also the viola capriccio; IMSLP list also gives Op. 61 for the same set).
IMSLP: Old England, Op. 42, "Caprice pour le violon, sur Airs anglais du 16me et 17me siècle" (1865), violin & orchestra with composer's piano arrangement. English subtitle is an accurate gloss.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: 4 Romances sans paroles, Op. 8 = Hilarité; Innocence; Barcarolle; Air savoyard (Troupenas 1846, first published as Op. 7 2nd suite). Hilarité.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: 4 Romances sans paroles, Op. 8 = Hilarité; Innocence; Barcarolle; Air savoyard (Troupenas 1846, first published as Op. 7 2nd suite). Innocence.

IMSLP: Scène et Romance de 'Halka' (Moniuszko), 1861, violin & orchestra (or piano); Wikipedia agrees.

verdicts.title: Souvenir de Donizetti (Fantaisie on 'Lucia di Lammermoor')
verdicts.note: IMSLP: Souvenir de Donizetti, Op.33 (alt. "Fantaisie sur Lucia de Lammermoor"; André, Offenbach 1856/57, plate 7788), but the Wikipedia list gives Op. 33 to the Bouquet américain and says the Lucia fantasy was merely "published as Op. 33" and has no opus. Opus dropped to avoid a duplicate.
IMSLP: Souvenir de Russie, fantaisie, Op. 21 (Kistner/Troupenas 1846), violin & orchestra or piano.
IMSLP: Souvenir d'Amitié (Romance), Op. 8bis (Schuberth, Hamburg 1867/1871). Not in Wikipedia list (which only mentions the 6 Morceaux de salon arrangement drawn from it); IMSLP only.
IMSLP: Suite, Op. 43, B minor (Preludio; Minuetto; Aria; Gavotte), Schuberth 1871; Wikipedia agrees.
IMSLP lists only 1834 autograph manuscripts (family archive, scans uploaded 2026; "first publication 2021"); no printed edition. Early manuscript-only work, so out of scope.
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Grande sonate concertante in D major, Op. 12 (Troupenas 1843).
IMSLP: Voix de cœur, Op. 53, nine pieces (Tendresse ... Thème et variations); Wikipedia spells "Voies de cœur" (posthumous).
IMSLP/Wikipedia: Voix intimes, Op. 45, six pensées mélodiques (Brandus 1876).

gaps.title: L'Orage, Op. 22 No. 6
gaps.note: No. 6 of the 6 Morceaux de salon; the pass-1 draft covered Nos. 1, 2, 4 and the existing catalogue has Nos. 3 and 5. Also listed in the Wikipedia work list.

gaps.title: Grand Duo on 'Preciosa'
gaps.note: Duo concertante No. 9 on Weber's Preciosa; sibling of the queued Grand Duo on 'Orphée' (plate 17556). Wikipedia list: 'Duo brillant sur Preciosa' (1864).

gaps.title: Grand duo brillant on 'Le camp de Silésie', Op. 24
gaps.note: On themes of Meyerbeer's Le camp de Silésie (Vielka); dedicated to General Lvov. Op. 24 is also the number of the Divertissements d'amateurs (N7).

gaps.title: Grande fantaisie on 'Oberon', Op. 14
gaps.edition: E. Troupenas (Paris) [c.1843], plate T. 1435; Brandus reprint
gaps.note: IMSLP: Duo concertant No. 2 on Weber's Oberon, dedicated to the Duc de Loos; Wikipedia list also gives Op. 14 (version for piano or orchestra).

gaps.title: Fantaisie concertante on 'Les Huguenots'
gaps.note: On Meyerbeer's Les Huguenots, E major, dedicated to Servais; listed with year 1838 in the Wikipedia work list.

gaps.title: Paul et Virginie (Duo)
gaps.note: Duo on Massé's opera Paul et Virginie, dedicated to Mlle Alix Massé; Wikipedia list agrees (c.1877).

existing_issues.issue: Op. 56 is the Fantaisie "Salut à l'Amérique" (Greeting to America) in E major for violin and orchestra, pub. c.1882 (Brandus, plate 12,811); IMSLP does not mention Yankee Doodle there. The "Yankee Doodle" variations are Op. 17 (Souvenirs d'Amérique, already id 2231), so the parenthetical looks like a mix-up.
